summary: IDS feed s056_single is degraded due to 23.2% duplicate packets (1006/4334, threshold 5%) exceeding tolerance; all other checks (one-way, drops, overload, encrypted share, VLAN) are healthy.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker is aggregating overlapping sources (e.g., multiple SPAN sessions or both sides of a TAP) without deduplication, forwarding the same packet multiple times to the IDS tool port. 23.2% duplicates indicates systematic broker-level duplication, not normal TCP retransmits.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS wastes CPU/memory re-processing identical packets and TCP stream reassembly is distorted. This inflates flow counts, can create duplicate/false alerts, and reduces effective inspection capacity for real threats despite IDS needing full payload and both directions.

recommended_fix.why: Enable packet-broker deduplication in a short time window to drop identical packets before delivery to the 1G IDS port, restoring correct traffic volume and freeing IDS resources for accurate detection without losing payload.
